summary: Rabbi Hidary goes through Masekhet Arachin, studying the calculation of Yovel cycles from the entry into the land of Israel, the minimum numbers for lambs and musical instruments in the Bet HaMikdash, and the laws of children singing with the Leviim. The class also begins the third perek, analyzing the leniencies and stringencies of Arakhin vows.
questions: How many Yovel cycles did Israel count from entering the land until the destruction of the Bet HaMikdash?
How many days in advance must the lambs for the Korban Tamid be inspected?
What instruments were played in the Bet HaMikdash and what were their minimum and maximum quantities?
Were minor children allowed into the courtyard of the Bet HaMikdash during the service?
How do the laws of Arakhin combine both leniency and stringency?
